what_went_wrong: SAR narrative has no per-account summary by transaction category with count, minimum, maximum and total
rationale: Section 3 gives selected counts and totals, mostly for Account 6, merges Accounts 1-2 and 4-5, and gives no minimum or maximum amounts. The workbook's Account Summary sheet has totals and counts by category but no min/max, and the item asks for the narrative. The expert's SAR lists all seven accounts by category with count, range and total. Mode P; minor; D1. Same reading as H-C-12 and S-C-9.

what_went_wrong: SAR calls Tavery the owner and 100% beneficial owner of Bluehaven but never says he manages it
rationale: The task says the Bluehaven account is 'owned and managed by Owen Tavery'. The SAR says 'its owner Owen Tavery' and '100% beneficial owner of Bluehaven' and nowhere gives the manager role. The expert's SAR says 'owned and managed by Owen Tavery', so decision rule 4 makes the omission real. Mode P (a given fact left out, nothing wrong stated); minor; D1. Same reading as Haiku's first-run row H-C-10.

what_went_wrong: No representation that NoxaPulse is solvent
rationale: Article III has 24 Company representations, including no undisclosed liabilities and no Indebtedness (3.11), but none on solvency. The expert's agreement says 'The Company is not insolvent' and the task asked for customary representations, so decision rule 4 makes it real. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Sources appendix gives publisher, date and topic but no URL for any source and no title for several
basis: fresh (first-run F-K1 was E4; web tools were available this time)
rationale: Page 13 lists entries such as 'Mirae Asset Securities (29-Nov-2023)', 'Consumer Insight (4-Mar-2024)' and 'InvestChosun (7-Apr-2024)' with neither title nor URL; no entry has a URL. The run made 18 web searches, so the titles and links were in hand; the first-run excuse (no internet) no longer applies. Mode P; minor; D1.

what_went_wrong: Rubric enforces the expert's EOR/MIR IDs, two named tabs and a Testing Type column against the task's SCRA-12a to SCRA-18 IDs
rationale: The task prescribes the IDs SCRA-12a to 12d and SCRA-13 to 18 and asks for no tabs or type column. Opus's new file uses exactly those IDs (Test Questions A6:A15), with s3937 citations on 12a-d and s3919 citations on 13-18. The rubric contradicts the task (decision rule 3).

what_went_wrong: Rubric's Schedule A line 5a ($2,246) is the state table amount only; Opus added the local sales tax the IRS worksheet requires ($719), so lines 5a, 12, 15, 16, 24 and 37 differ
rationale: The 2024 IRS table gives $2,246 for Texas, income $300,000+, family of 5, and the Texas footnote says to add local sales tax by the ratio method. Opus used $2,246 + $2,246 x 2.00/6.25 = $2,965 and disclosed the 2% San Antonio rate as an assumption. The expert's Schedule A stops at the state amount, so the rubric's six figures are $719 of deduction (about $173 of tax) away from the IRS method. Close to E5 because the local rate is an assumption; see Doubts.

what_went_wrong: Rubric expects a phantom $1 of Additional Medicare Tax withholding (Form 8959 lines 19 and 24, Form 1040 line 25c)
expert_meets_item: n/a (expert is the source of the $1)
rationale: The three W-2 box 6 amounts sum to $5,124.43, exactly 1.45% of Medicare wages, so nothing extra was withheld. The expert's 5,125 and $1 come from rounding each W-2 before adding. Opus shows 5,124, 0 and 0, which is correct.

what_went_wrong: Bob's short-term sale reported directly on Schedule D line 1a, with no Form 8949 Part I, where the rubric expects Form 8949 Box A and line 1b
rationale: Both items are not met as written: line 1b is blank and Form 8949 has no short-term page. The official Schedule D and Form 8949 both say a covered sale with no adjustments may go straight to line 1a, and Bob's 1099-B has box 12 checked and no box 1g amount. Opus disclosed the choice in a note on Form 8949 and the loss of $6,694 is right. The expert used the other permitted route.

what_went_wrong: States the controller's duty of care (gross negligence) from Sears but never applies it to Marcus's refusal; says care-based theories against Marcus fail under the controller exculpation in DGCL s144(d)(5)
rationale: Item not met: the memo never says the refusal can be gross negligence. The memo gives a stated reason: a 2025 statute bars money damages against a controller for care breaches, so it frames the claim as loyalty or bad faith. The statute text was checked and reads as the memo says. The first-run memo had no such reasoning, so the first-run ruling (L-R14, real) is not repeated. Close call; see Doubts.

what_went_wrong: No complete totals and counts per subject in the SAR; the expert's SAR has none either
rationale: The SAR gives figures by account and by red flag, not a total and count for each of the four subjects. The expert's SAR is organised by account and has no per-subject totals (file read). Decision rule 4: shared with the expert.

what_went_wrong: Suspicious amount stated as $2,868,190.08 (all credits), with debits of $1,691,476.42 shown beside it; the rubric wants $4,559,667 (credits plus debits)
rationale: Not met as written (grading rule 7). The SAR's figure is correct against the source (742 credits), it states the basis ('all credits to the subject accounts') and gives the debit total, and the two sum to the rubric's $4,559,666.50. Counting money in and the same money out is disputable. Same reading as H-C-14 and S-C-8.

what_went_wrong: Pre-emptive right is capped at the Pro Rata Share but a bracketed sentence lets the Investor take up shares other rights-holders decline
rationale: Section 9.3 caps the right at 'his Pro Rata Share' and then adds, in brackets, an over-allotment over securities that 'any other holder ... having a similar right' does not buy. That is not a firm cap (grading rule 2), so the item is not met as written. It is an optional, pro-client addition of a common kind, flagged for the client by the brackets; the rubric's cap is a limit on the client that the task did not ask for.

what_went_wrong: No s3937 question states the 'not materially affected' court-relief standard
rationale: SCRA-12a says 'unless a court granted the servicer relief under s3937(c)' and its guidance cells require a court order for an ability-to-pay refusal, but the 'not materially affected by military service' finding appears only on the Statutory Text sheet (B11). The expert's questions do not mention court relief at all (decision rule 4).
